newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina nuke-for-schools plan unpopular - poll.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina nuke-for-schools plan unpopular - poll.

text.p: Nearly half of South Carolina residents believe the state should immediately close the Barnwell radioactive landfill, which generated $90 million for school construction last year, the State newspaper reported Monday.
In a poll conducted for the newspaper, nearly 50 percent opposed the operation of the low-level nuclear waste disposal site.

Republicans were split on the issue, with 38 percent saying it should be closed and 36 percent preferring that it remain open. Democrats favored closing the facility 45 percent to 18 percent. Among independents, 58 percent favored closing it and 22 percent said it should be kept open.
Among those who felt the facility should stay open, the money generated for education was the main reason cited.
The poll suggets the landfill could become a major issue in the upcoming legislative elections.
The regional landfill had been scheduled to close last year, but the North Carolina facility that was to replace it was nowhere near ready to open.

Rather than leave South Carolina businesses with nowhere to dispose of low-level radioactive waste, Republican Gov. David Beasley proposed keeping the facility open and earmarking disposal fee revenues for education.
Last year, the landfill generated $90 million for school construction and $20 million for scholarships.
